purpose: The five questions of re-research-3.md, run. Three read behaviour left in public artefacts; two are experiments we ran on this machine.
note: Rounds 1 and 2 read what people wrote, and rule 5 governs all of it. Q-F and Q-J are a different class: the observation is ours, so the mark covers the behaviour and not the utterance. Q-G, Q-H and Q-I read diffs, blob SHAs and commit dates, which are also behaviour. Every count below is re-runnable from the query beside it.

instruments.name: The handover test - we ran it
instruments.what: A composed archive of ten real pinned items, containing five planted defects, handed to three fresh receiving agents with one instruction.
instruments.blind_to: What a human recipient does; other vendors (Cursor and Codex CLIs are not installed on this machine); whether anybody would reach for such an archive unprompted. It is three model tiers of one agent, on one machine, on one day.

instruments.name: GitHub forks + compare API across the fork point
instruments.what: ahead_by, the commits unique to the fork, and the files they touched.
instruments.blind_to: Motive; private handovers, which never appear as a fork; anybody who is not on GitHub. A fork is a public, self-selecting act.

instruments.name: git/trees blob SHAs, then full history over duplicated paths
instruments.what: Whether two copies of one item are byte-identical now, and for how long they have differed.
instruments.blind_to: Whether the divergence cost anybody anything; private repositories; a copy deliberately kept different is indistinguishable from one forgotten.

instruments.name: npm registry download series + GitHub code search for vendored files
instruments.what: Whether installing other people's material is a recurring behaviour, and whether what was imported is ever touched again.
instruments.blind_to: Private use; who the person was; a download is not a use, and `npx` re-downloads on every invocation, so downloads are closer to invocations than to people.

instruments.name: Run the competitors
instruments.what: What the tools whose READMEs claim duplicate audit, drift detection and trust scores actually detect, pointed at the same deliberately broken set as Q-F.
instruments.blind_to: Funded closed products behind a login; roadmaps; anything they do for paying customers.

planted_defects: MCP key collision `memory` at two refs
discovered_defects_not_planted: @anthropic/mcp-github and @anthropic/mcp-memory do not exist on npm
the pdf skill references REFERENCE.md, FORMS.md and scripts/ that were never exported
the surviving settings.json hooks call .claude/hooks/skill-eval.sh, in no item

limits: Every count over public repositories over-samples people who publish. The one practitioner ever interviewed keeps this material in a private repository.
Q-F is three model tiers of one vendor's agent on one machine on one day, not three vendors in clean containers. Cursor and Codex CLIs are not installed here.
Q-J ran read-only verbs only. No tool was asked to install or modify anything.
The GitHub code search API caps at 100 results per page and was read one page deep per phrase, so the vendored-copy sample is 100 per skill against total_counts in the thousands.
